summary.name: DropKeeper
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source, fully offline macOS menu bar app that gives each new download an expiry time and moves expired files to the Trash, with History to restore them.
use_cases: Keep the Desktop and Downloads folders tidy
Set a timed expiry on installers and screenshots
Restore a file that was moved to the Trash by mistake
Use a file manager that makes no network connections
summary.what_it_does: When a file lands in a watched folder (Downloads by default, Desktop or others can be added), a small prompt appears under the menu bar icon where you choose to keep it or have it expire after 30 minutes, an hour, a day, ten days, or a configurable time. Expired files move to the Trash, and History lists the last 10 decisions so files can be put back. Optional rules match files by type, name pattern or folder and assign expiry automatically; reminders warn before a file goes, and duplicates of files already in the folder are flagged. The app makes no network connections, and statistics about handled files are computed locally.
notable: Fully offline: no analytics, no update checks, no networking code, enforced by CI
Expired files go to the Trash, never permanently deleted; Undo button for manual deletes
Rules-based automatic expiry by file type, name pattern or folder; starter rules ship off
MIT licensed; available in English, Czech, German, Spanish and French
caveats: Not notarized by Apple, so Gatekeeper may block it unless installed via the Homebrew cask or the README steps are followed
History only shows the last 10 decisions
